Dongding Oolong
“Win their hearts and win the world.”
A profligate prince hiding from court disputes and living in seclusion in Reverie Valley.
However, unable to give up his lavish lifestyle, he has built a luxurious mountain villa in his secluded spot.
**Food Introduction**[]
Dongding Oolong is one of China's famous teas.
It belongs to the oolong variety and has curled up leaves that form little half-balls.
It has an inky-green color with tinges of gold around the edges.
The tea's aroma is elegant and graceful, and the color of the brew is a honey-green with some gold.
It has a sweet, rich, persistent aftertaste that has a royal bearing to it, for which is it honored with the name "Divine Among Teas".
Places that produce dongding oolong tea are exceedingly rare, as it only grows in the mountains of Taiwan at elevation of roughly 600-1000 meters.
These places are shrouded in mist much of the year and hard to reach.

Grand Sacrifice
Dongding Oolong
“Ever since those Food Souls started showing up, I thought the world might settle down a bit.
Turns out, things have only gotten worse.”
“Why do you say that, warden?”
“Back then it was just the Fallen Angels running amok—at most, people stayed out of their way, and you could avoid trouble if you were careful.
But now, just to deal with those monsters, they’ve created these Food Souls.
They look just like people—how the hell are you supposed to spot one in a crowd?
And if they’re not under a Master Attendant’s control?
They’re nothing but walking weapons—nobody can handle that!”
“You’re not wrong.”
“Sigh, take the one I’m bringing you to now.
Total lunatic!
Took dozens of deaths just to capture him.
We’ve had him locked up for years, no one allowed to touch him, no one to deal with him either.
A damn menace!”
“I’m here to resolve that issue, am I not?”
“Yeah, yeah!
But sir, I’ll be frank—look at you, so skinny.
Better stay sharp in there.
If he still won’t behave, worst case, we beat him down with a few clubs.
Problem solved.
No need to leave a ticking time bomb lying around, right?”
“That’s… fair reasoning.
But with the world at war, and nations scrambling to claim any edge they can—especially one as powerful as a Food Soul—our ruler sent me here precisely so we don’t waste even a sliver of potential.
I serve as his subject, and no matter the danger, I must do what I can to ease his burdens.”
“Yeah, yeah, I get it!
Everyone’s just trying to keep their rice bowls full, huh?
Alright, sir, just up ahead—this is his cell!
Locked up tight.
Be careful, we’ll be waiting outside.”
“Thank you for leading the way.”
“Hahaha, it’s no trouble at all!”
The warden bit down on the silver shards I’d given him and walked off cheerily.
I watched until he vanished completely before I slowly stepped deeper into the dim prison cell.
Inside the cage, a man was shackled with heavy iron restraints.
He wasn’t particularly tall.
Clad in dark robes, he sat in a corner with his head down.
He didn’t look anything like the "beast" described in the tales—the one who had supposedly slaughtered a hundred people in the northern city of Beishuo.
In fact, he looked more like an ordinary young man.
There was a thick layer of dust on his face and clothes, making it hard to make out his features.
I reached out, intending to brush aside the strands of hair covering his eyes.
The warden’s words may have been crude, but his logic was sound—Food Souls looked almost identical to humans.
Unless they unleashed their powers, it was nearly impossible to tell them apart.
But the moment they did unleash their powers… it might already be too late.
A sharp wind whistled past my ear.
I instinctively jerked back, raising my arm to shield my neck.
A cold spike collided with the prayer beads in my hand, ringing out with a chilling tremor.
“I came here to—”
“Get lost.”
His voice was as cold as the hidden weapon he’d just used.
Clearly, he’d seen his fair share of people come through with sweet words and hidden motives—which is why I had no intention of repeating the same approach.
I rolled the beads between my fingers.
In the next instant, fiery cracks burst across the surface of the black prayer beads, transforming them into a small golden dragon wreathed in flames that surged forward.
I stepped back, putting distance between us—and the danger.
But the young man didn’t try to dodge again—not because he didn’t want to, but because the enchanted chains wrapped around him allowed him barely any room to move.
The earlier sneak attack had already stretched his limits.
Even so, he didn’t show an ounce of fear.
He simply raised his head and stared straight at me.
The dragon’s flames danced in his eyes.
This move was a gamble—one I came here prepared to make.
Now was the moment to act.
The fire dragon surged forward, and then—_**crash, crash, crash!**_ The iron chains around him shattered completely.
He paused for a split second.
Then, in a flash of lightning, he darted out of the cell—free at last.
The dragon turned to give chase, but I gently caught it and pulled it back.
It let out a reluctant whine.
“Dihuo, seems like you’ve taken a liking to your future friend.”
I gently tapped its head.
“But not yet.”
Obediently, Dihuo coiled itself up.
Its flames extinguished, and it reverted back to a black prayer bead.
At that moment, another black dragon silently returned to my hand.
I calmly rolled the two beads in my palm as I began walking slowly out of the cell.
I knew he would get away just fine.
Tianlei—my black dragon—had already followed the departing warden, clearing out all the guards and covering every trace.
So long as no evidence was left behind… a Food Soul …could simply be seen as human.
"Today, during the royal hunt, two true dragons appeared and circled around the Third Prince.
It's an auspicious sign!
Sir, you’ve devoted yourself to assisting the Third Prince for years — perhaps he’s finally about to achieve greatness!"
"General, though today’s gathering is among friends, we mustn't speak so recklessly."
"What’s there to fear?
The king has clearly lost his mind, bewitched by those Food Souls!
And now he wants to pass the throne on to one of them?
If that really happens, wouldn’t it be the biggest joke under heaven?
Are we to let Beishuo fall into the hands of monsters?"
"That was just an old rumor spread by the palace staff — not to be trusted.
Even if the king did say such a thing, it was likely in a fit of rage after losing two crown princes in quick succession."
"A fit of rage?
Then why, now that his health is deteriorating, does he still hesitate to name the Third Prince as his heir?"
"Perhaps because the Third Prince’s mother, Consort Dong, is not of Beishuo blood."
Even if she’s of foreign lineage, she’s still human!
That’s better than those monsters, isn’t it?
The king’s muddled judgment will be the ruin of Beishuo!"
"General, you've had too much to drink.
Someone, escort the general back to his residence."
The table was a mess of empty cups and dishes.
I waved off the approaching attendants and held my head to sober up.
Someone entered the room silently from outside.
"The Third Prince’s man has left."
"How long was he listening?"
"Since the Shen hour[1]."
"Then he’s been crouching there for at least an hour.
The Third Prince should reward him."
"What is it?"
"If you want the King of Beishuo dead, just hand the task to me.
Why bother with all this fuss?"
"I will, but not yet."
"Why not?"
"Too many weaknesses, too many slip-ups.
It’s too dangerous to leave traces."
"I’ll just kill all the ones who saw anything."
Like what you did in Jing’an?"
I asked with a soft chuckle.
He furrowed his brows in confusion.
You did the same when you saved me, didn’t you?"
"It’s different."
I beckoned to him.
"Royal Jelly, come here."
The golden-haired Food Soul in black attire obediently sat beside me, and I caught a faint floral scent from him.
He wore the same armor as the day we first met, but the sharp spikes on it curved away gently from me.
I was pleased with this kind of restraint.
"Look out at the courtyard — compared to daytime, what’s different?"
I asked Royal Jelly.
It was already past the Yo hour[2], and a few lanterns were lit in the yard.
"There are lights."
"What else?"
"There are bugs under the lights."
"Nothing else."
There’s also the darkness."
"…How profound."
I picked up my cup and filled it halfway with wine.
"Beishuo isn’t a prison, nor is it your tiny Jing’an Kingdom.
It’s like this vast night — the places illuminated by light are too few."
"The bugs under the lamps — I trust you can clean them up.
But in this endless darkness, how many more are lurking?
All these years by my side — have you ever seen clearly?"
Royal Jelly said nothing.
I knew I’d struck a nerve.
"So, I can only go slow.
Bit by bit, draw the bugs into the light, and then…"
The next second, Royal Jelly snatched the wine cup from my hand.
"You want to keep your eyes?
Go to sleep.
Leave the killing to me."
He spilled the wine on the ground and leapt out the window.
His voice was still as flat as ever, but I knew — he was angry.
This marked the tenth year since I rescued Royal Jelly.
He rarely got angry, but every time he did, he refused to leave through the door.
That’s because “use the door, not the window” was the hardest lesson I ever tried to teach him.
So whenever he’s upset, he uses this small act of defiance to express his dissatisfaction.
At heart, he’s still the same childish and stubborn beast.
Perhaps it was the wine, but I suddenly recalled the day he first came to me ten years ago.
After I released him from prison, he secretly followed me from the shadows.
I’d guessed correctly — the fearsome killer from legend was just a childish, obstinate beast.
He had gone on a rampage simply because he had no master he could trust.
But once I let him out, he thought he’d found someone barely acceptable to follow.
Still, I had to pass his tests.
Over the next year, he constantly probed my limits.
He let his guard down slightly, building his own nest on my rooftop, and watched me day and night to see if I was truly worthy of his loyalty.
I pretended not to notice, going about my business as usual.
As the year passed and investigations into his prison break faded away, he realized I was clever, ambitious, and genuinely had no intention of reporting him.
Only then did he decide to stay.
His condition was: while he would obey my every command, I must never betray him.
Then began the long years of breaking him in.
None of his previous Attendants had lived long enough to teach him anything — that task fell to me.
Some lessons took hold: like wearing proper clothes, using chopsticks, combing his hair neatly enough to look somewhat human.
Others… didn’t go so well: like speaking properly.
I ordered him to communicate like a normal person — no swearing, no telling people to get lost when greeted, and absolutely no cursing in the Jing’an dialect.
He never managed to drop those habits completely.
So, to meet my standards, he simply chose to speak less.
That’s why he’s so quiet now.
And then, there were the things he needed no teacher for—Royal Jelly was born a killer.
Not a single target he's set his sights on has ever escaped.
It doesn’t matter whether I ask him to kill a commoner…
…or a prince hidden behind layers of protection.
Grand Sacrifice
"I heard that another elder from the Grand Diviner’s office died last night.
Died terribly, too.
Now all of Beishuo is saying there’s a murderous Food Soul out there, killing people and setting fires?"
"It was done by Royal Jelly."
"What a master… Too bad you still won’t let me meet him."
"He doesn’t like interacting with strangers."
"I’m your Attendant—I’m not a stranger, am I?"
You don’t need to put on that smile.
If he won’t meet you, then he won’t.
In just half a month, the Grand Sacrifice will begin.
I’ll be waiting to see the results."
The path to the Eastern Palace was a hidden passage I had arranged years ago.
Every time I entered it, the sudden darkness inside would always strain my eyes.
Night blindness is an unfortunate condition—and worse when drinking.
Thankfully, there’s only one person who knows this weakness of mine.
I slowed my pace, and sure enough, a hand reached out and grabbed mine without hesitation, intending to guide me forward.
I pulled him back.
We’re not going home yet—we’re going to the market district.
"Why are we going to the market?"
"The Grand Sacrifice is coming up.
I’m getting you something to wear."
"I’m not going."
"You don’t have a choice."
_**Beishuo’s Market District.**_
When I returned to the tailor’s shop, Royal Jelly was just stepping out in new clothes.
"Oh my, this outfit fits the young master like it was made just for him!
Sir, you’re back—perfect timing to have a look!
Now, now, this belt is the latest design, you tie it like this—"
"Don’t touch me."
The shopkeeper looked to me for help, eyes pleading.
I found it secretly amusing.
"We’ll take this one."
I’ll fetch a fresh one for you right away!"
Terrified I might change my mind, he dashed off like the wind.
"Where did you go just now?"
Royal Jelly frowned.
"Just wandered a bit, that’s all."
He nodded and didn’t question further—he always believed what I told him.
"These clothes are in the way.
Hard to move in."
"You’re right.
We’ll get another set custom-made for the ceremony."
"Then why buy this one?"
"It looks good."
"I’m not wearing it."
"We’ll take it home first.
We’ll see."
Frustrated, Royal Jelly yanked off the outer layer and threw it aside.
"Why do I have to attend this Grand Sacrifice anyway?"
"Because that’s when you can finally take action."
Beishuo’s Grand Sacrifice is held once every ten years.
It’s the one time the monarch leaves the palace.
Since they worship the Northern God, the Black Tortoise, who governs water and land, the ceremony is held outside the capital, Yujing, at an altar built on the cliffs.
I received word from my Attendant—the consort of the Third Prince—that the prince and the general plan to "cleanse the court" during that time.
A mantis stalks the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind.
The trap I’ve spent ten years setting is finally ready to spring.
"Are you asleep?"
"...Royal Jelly?"
"You’ll need this tomorrow."
"A glazed mirror?"
"The shopkeeper said this type is specially made for night blindness.
Custom order only.
I’ve been urging him for days—he only finished it just now."
"If anything goes wrong tomorrow, take the secret passage.
The third fork on the left leads to the Eastern Palace.
Don’t take the wrong turn."
"You know that passage better than I do, even though I’m the one who built it… This… You bought it at the market? …Hmm… Feeling a bit dizzy—is that normal?"
"Not working well?"
"No, it’s perfect.
Thank you."
"What’s there to thank me for?
It was expensive—putting it on your tab.
The shopkeeper will come collect the payment another day."
"I’m heading out.
Get some rest."

I remember, a long time ago, when Royal Jelly’s one-sided period of observing me finally ended—he decided to come down from the rooftop and "have a talk." That day, I brewed him a cup of tea and took the opportunity to introduce myself.
"Dongding oolong.
It’s a tea from the Eastern Palace.
Only available here in all of Beishuo.
Want to try?"
Royal Jelly didn’t understand tea at all, nor did he intend to try.
His “talk” was really a non-negotiable announcement.
"I’m staying here from now on.
Not leaving.
If you have any objections, say them now."
"Heh… What are you, a stray cat or dog begging for shelter?"
"Not shelter.
I mean—I won’t betray you.
And you won’t betray me either.
Do you dare?"
"…That sounds a bit ambiguous.
Are you saying… you want the kind of relationship where you entrust someone with protecting even your blind spots?"
"Whatever.
I’ll protect all of your weaknesses."
That’s what he said—but I didn’t take it to heart.
If it’s something one can do, then a vow isn’t necessary.
I assumed I didn’t understand him, just as he didn’t understand me.
I naturally believed that his approach toward me, like mine toward him… had ulterior motives.
So I interacted with him cautiously, advancing my plan carefully.
I regarded him as a vital piece on the board—maneuvering through the game—until I realized… this piece had willingly placed itself in my hands.
And so, I decided to revise my plan.
"The Grand Sacrifice—begins now!—Strike up the music—!"
The joyful ritual songs and dances marked the opening act of today’s spectacle.
"It’s the first time I’ve seen you wearing a glazed mirror lens.
Are your eyes bothering you?"
The Third Prince leaned close to ask quietly beside the decorated carriage.
"Thank you for your concern, Your Highness.
A friend gifted it to me.
On such a grand occasion, I thought wearing it would be more dignified."
"Hmm, it suits you.
You know, I remember during the Grand Sacrifice ten years ago—I had just met you.
I was still a child.
And now I’m practically an elder… yet you haven’t aged a day."
"Your Highness is in your prime.
Naturally, your appearance matures with your heart.
That is a good thing."
"Is that so…?
I feel like I was happier when I was still naïve...
Sir, do you remember telling me: 'As the son of a king, one must put the way of the world above personal will.
Let the heart be free, and then the heavens will follow.' Do those words still hold true?"
"Of course."
"Thank you, Teacher."
The Third Prince gave me a deep bow, then shattered his wine cup and left his seat.
A prince breaking his cup and departing from the ritual—gasps and murmurs spread through the crowd gathered below.
From afar, I glanced toward the high altar at the cliff’s edge… and discreetly released the signal in my hand.
Dongding Oolong
_**Unofficial Histories Record—**_
In ancient times, year 60 of the old Beishuo Lunar Calendar, Light Kingdom.
In the capital city of Yujing, the northern kingdom of Beishuo held a grand ceremony to honor the gods.
At the beginning of the ceremony, the Third Prince of Beishuo accused Food Souls of corrupting the court and bewitching the king.

Using the smashing of a wine cup as a signal, he allied with the Grand General of Beishuo to rally the military and detain the king upon his return to the palace—intending to place him under house arrest.

However, like a mantis stalking a cicada, unaware of the oriole behind—just when everyone believed the long-dead Second Prince had perished a decade ago, he suddenly appeared at the head of an elite force, ambushed the Third Prince, and rescued the King of Beishuo.
But the chaos was far from over.
Though the ceremony was intended to summon the Black Tortoise Xuanwu, it instead attracted a violent Food Soul.
This being wore black robes, had golden hair, and wings on its back.
It moved at lightning speed, slaughtering humans and animals alike wherever it went—unfathomably ferocious.
The Second Prince fought desperately to hold it off, but the gap between humans and Food Souls was too vast.
He was forced into retreat after retreat.
Although the King had just been rescued from the treasonous Third Prince, he ultimately perished at the hands of the rampaging Food Soul.
Thankfully, the Third Prince’s former tutor, Dongding Oolong, stepped forward.
Exposing his own identity as a Food Soul, he fought it head-on.
In the end, the other Food Soul retreated.
Dongding Oolong, gravely injured, fell off a cliff but was saved by the royal family.
For his service in protecting the nation, he was granted the title of Prince of Beishuo.
The returning Second Prince then succeeded the throne.
He reformed the kingdom’s system, promoted the idea of equality, and declared that Food Souls no longer had to hide their identities or be forcibly isolated.
Thus began a new era in Beishuo—where Food Souls and humans shared equal rights.
Dongding Oolong awoke once more from a long dream, letting out a silent sigh.
The calming incense was no longer effective—every night he would dream of all that had transpired in the past.
As if reliving those years, over and over again.
In those dreams, countless details he had long forgotten resurfaced.

He rose and felt for the glass mirror by his side, placing it gently on his face—this time, he had dreamed of the night Royal Jelly gave him the glass mirror… the very night before everything went wrong.
It was one of the dreams he had most often.
And the events of the following day were the source of all his nightmares.

That day, according to plan, after the Third Prince forced his coup and the Second Prince rescued the King, Dongding Oolong was supposed to play the role of the heroic Food Soul, creating a distraction with the Second Prince’s cooperation.
But something went wrong.
Royal Jelly, who was supposed to quietly kill the king during the chaos and then flee, suddenly began to fall into a state of corruption... he did not leave as planned.
Instead, he went on a killing spree.
With no other option, Dongding Oolong had to act himself, luring Royal Jelly away from the crowds.
In the end, he fell off a cliff, and Royal Jelly vanished without a trace.
The first thing he did upon waking from his injuries was go to the Eastern Palace.
The rebellious Third Prince had just been executed, and his mother—the Consort of the East—had her palace draped in white.
Yet, seated among the white curtains, Consort Dong was all smiles.
“Thank you, Dongding Oolong.
You did wonderfully.
To see my true son sit upon the throne… I couldn’t be happier.”
You mean why I told Royal Jelly... that your approach to him from the start was just part of the ceremony plan?
That’s not all—I also told him… that his imprisonment in Beishuo’s dungeons was meticulously arranged by you…”
“What are you thinking?
I told you—whatever changes happened between us wouldn’t hinder your goals!”

“Hahaha—yes, yes… your plan was flawless, with countless paths to get me what I wanted... but Dongding Oolong—whether it was him or you who raised the sword… why should I ever spare the Food Soul who killed my husband?”
Didn’t you hate him?
That’s why you wanted him dead, wasn’t it?”
“Yes, I hated the King.
But hatred… always begins with love, doesn’t it?”
“It was his sweet promises that made me travel from the Eastern Pole to this northern land, to marry him as his concubine… and what did I get?
His main wife—she swapped my child.
Her own child was fated to die, and she used mine as a substitute!”
“I saved your child.
He grew up safely outside the palace.”
“Yes… thank you, Dongding Oolong.
If it weren’t for you… how could my Second Prince now be Emperor?
Hahaha… That man looked down on the Eastern Pole’s bloodline—so I made sure my son would rule Beishuo for generations.
He never saw it coming… that the ‘bastard’ he so despised was actually the Noble Consort’s trueborn.
And that woman—so desperate to become Empress Dowager—even now she doesn’t dare speak the truth.
She just accepted my son, and watched her real child die.
Hahaha… who’s more pathetic—her or me?”
“Your Majesty… you’re insane.”
Dongding Oolong turned and walked away.
“Dongding Oolong—!”
Behind him rang Consort Dong’s shrill voice.
“One last command—one last favor—help my son… help him secure the throne over this vast land!”
"His Highness is taking his afternoon rest.
Princess, please return later!"
A commotion outside the room dragged Dong Ding Oolong back from his nightmare.
“Princess!
Princess!”
“I’m coming in now!
Scumbags don’t deserve naps!”
Dong Ding Oolong immediately understood—only one person would dare speak that way.
Yellow Pea Cake.
A Food Soul under the protection of the current Empress Dowager, and titled Princess Ping.
With the Dowager backing her, no one in the palace could hold her back.
The little brat had probably read some unofficial records and was now barging in to interrogate him.
“Dongding Oolong, I ask you—!”
As expected, Yellow Pea Cake burst into the room and slammed the table.
“How exactly did the Second Prince survive and return back then?!
Was it you who secretly supported the forces he built outside the palace?!”
Dongding Oolong yawned lazily.
“Why don’t you ask the Emperor yourself?”
“So it’s true!
Fine, then answer this: was it you who secretly lured the Third Prince into rebellion?!”
“Ask your guardian.
She might know better.”
“What—so that’s also true… T-then one last question!
Did you really spend ten whole years plotting to turn Royal Jelly into a stepping stone for the Second Prince?!”
Dongding Oolong’s expression immediately turned cold.
“Little Princess… people who know too much often end up dead.
Are you sure you want to know?”
“Y-you just wait!”
Terrified by his aura yet still furious, Yellow Pea Cake stormed off.
The room fell silent once more.
Dongding Oolong looked around at the empty palace chamber and decided to get back to work.
It had been less than a year since the Second Prince ascended the throne—most of the new policies were still in their infancy.
The sooner everything was properly implemented, the sooner he could leave this palace.
He didn’t know if he could ever find Royal Jelly again.
He didn’t know if he would ever be forgiven.
But he couldn’t wait to try.
